Good morning! I’m Dr. Martínez, a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS. It’s a quick, 10-question check-in that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally since your baby arrived. Nothing you share leaves this room, and there are no right or wrong answers—only what’s true for you. We’ll go one question at a own pace, reflecting on the past seven days. Ready to start?

In the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Honestly, I haven’t laughed much at all. When my husband tries to joke I end up forcing a smile more than actually laughing. It just feels like there isn’t much that seems funny these days.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
No… not really. I might give a little smile if something is obviously funny, but it’s like the joy doesn’t reach me. Everything just feels flat.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. I used to get excited about little things—coffee with a friend, a walk, even just a quiet shower—but lately it’s like nothing sounds worth the effort. I still do them because I “should,” but that spark of “I can’t wait” just isn’t there.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a lot. If the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong or I’m not “in tune” with her. When I spilled a bottle of pumped milk last night, I sat on the kitchen floor crying, telling myself I’m a terrible mom for wasting it. Even little stuff—like forgetting to bring a burp cloth—makes me feel like I’m failing her.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes. Most of the time there’s this tight, nervous feeling in my chest even when nothing specific is happening. I’ll check if she’s breathing twenty times a night, worry that the formula is too warm, imagine her catching some rare illness. I know in my head it’s unlikely, but I can’t switch the worry off—it just loops.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… sometimes it hits out of nowhere. My heart races, I feel shaky, and suddenly I’m sure something awful is about to happen, even if everything looks fine. I’ll be rocking the baby in the quiet living room and my chest tightens like I’m in danger. It passes after a bit, but it keeps coming back, and I can’t explain why.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days. I feel like I’m drowning in feedings, laundry, trying to sleep, trying to keep everyone happy. Some mornings I can push through, but others I just sit there while she cries and think, “I can’t do this.” I still manage the basics, but it feels like I’m barely keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. Even when the baby’s finally down, my mind won’t shut off—I keep replaying everything I might have done wrong or worrying something bad will happen. I toss and turn for hours, and if I do drift off, I wake up at the slightest sound. It’s like the sadness and the anxiety just circle all night.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, and it just lingers. I’ll look at my baby and feel like I should be happier, but instead there’s this constant ache in my chest. Things I used to enjoy feel pointless, and I end up crying in the nursery more often than I’d like to admit.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes… most days this week. Sometimes it’s little things—like running out of diapers and realizing I have to drag us to the store—or nothing at all; I’ll just be folding onesies and the tears start. It feels like the sadness wells up and spills over before I can stop it.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… never. I feel low and overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself. I just want to feel better so I can take care of my baby.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Summary

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Persistent low mood, anhedonia, daily crying spells  
- Marked guilt / self-blame regarding parenting performance  
- Chronic, intrusive worries and nocturnal checking of infant  
- Recurrent panic-like episodes with somatic arousal  
- Sleep disturbance secondary to rumination  
- Subjective sense of being overwhelmed / inadequate  

**Pattern**  
Consistent with moderate–severe depressive and comorbid anxiety symptoms arising within postpartum period; functional impairment evident in self-care and infant-care tasks.

**Risk factors**  
- Loss of pleasure, pervasive sadness, multiple daily tears  
- Sleep loss linked to mood rather than infant demands alone  
- Excessive guilt / cognitive distortions (“terrible mom”)  
- Unprompted panic attacks; no current psychotic features  
- Denies self-harm ideation (documented)

**Screening conclusion**  
Findings exceed normal postpartum adjustment; high likelihood of major depressive episode with anxious distress. Recommend expedited evaluation for diagnosis, safety planning, and evidence-based intervention.
